anomaly_def.Name: Database Memory Allocation Anomaly + Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Database Memory Allocation Anomaly : Excessive or unconstrained growth of database engine memory regions (buffer cache, work areas, plan cache, etc.) that pushes the host into sustained memory pressure, paging, or OOM scenarios.
Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly : Physical corruption or logical inconsistency inside on-disk data and index pages, causing checksums, key order, or page link verification to fail and making persisted structures unreliable.

When both root causes are present, the system may show a compound symptom set: 1) escalating memory consumption and swap activity, 2) intermittent or repeated detection of checksum or index-order errors, 3) erratic query plans that oscillate between index scans and full scans, 4) crash-recovery or instance-eviction cycles that arise from OOM killers or corruption panics, 5) heavy buffer churn as the engine attempts to reread or repair damaged pages, amplifying cache-miss rates and memory allocations, and 6) longer maintenance windows because integrity-check, repair, or restore tasks run concurrently with memory-hungry workloads, further stressing RAM.

Causal interaction: runaway memory allocations shrink the effective buffer cache and push clean pages out, increasing I/O and the likelihood that already-corrupted pages are reread and dereferenced. Every emergency checkpoint or abrupt shutdown triggered by OOM heightens the risk that partially flushed dirty buffers leave pages in an inconsistent state, deepening corruption. Conversely, encountering corrupted pages forces the engine to allocate extra diagnostic and recovery work areas, inflate error queues, and potentially pin suspect pages, all of which consume additional memory and aggravate the original memory pressure. The feedback loop between memory exhaustion and structural corruption accelerates system instability, turning what would be isolated faults into widespread service degradation and potential data loss.

entry.official_description: Cannot add foreign key on the base column of indexed virtual column.
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with logical data inconsistency, structural corruption, uniqueness conflicts, or referential-integrity rules being violated by the workload or storage state.
entry.solution_guidance: Validate data consistency, inspect constraints and index integrity, and check whether data-cleaning, repair, or workload correction is required before retrying.
